usage: Used in everyday situations to indicate that you are currently occupied or have a lot of work. It is standard across all Levantine dialects and is appropriate for both formal and casual contexts. The adjective must agree with the gender of the speaker.

variants.label: female speaker
variants.note: Used when the speaker is a woman.

variants.label: plural speaker
variants.note: Used when speaking on behalf of a group.

variants.label: emphasized
variants.note: Used by a male speaker to emphasize that he is extremely busy.

variants.label: common alternative
variants.note: A very common way to excuse yourself by stating you have tasks to do.

responses.english: May God give you health (Good job / Keep at it)

examples.arabic: آسف، ما فيني إحكي هلأ، أنا مشغول.
examples.transliteration: aasef, ma feeni e7ki hala2, ana mashghoul.
examples.english: Sorry, I can't talk right now, I'm busy.

examples.arabic: أنا كتير مشغول اليوم، خلينا نلتقي بكرا.
examples.transliteration: ana kteer mashghoul el yom, khalleena nelta2i bukra.
examples.english: I'm very busy today, let's meet tomorrow.

examples.arabic: هي ما إجت عالحفلة لأنها مشغولة.
examples.english: She didn't come to the party because she's busy.
